title: Vancomycin Trough Levels and Acute Kidney Injury Risk: A Meta-Analysis
author: Ioannis Bellos
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcctiswn
materials: Key-words: vancomycin trough nephrotoxicity acute kidney injury meta-analysis

steps.title: Search for Relevant Studies
steps.instruction: Systematically search specified databases and reference lists using defined key-terms to identify potential studies.

substeps.instruction: Search MEDLINE, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar.
Search reference lists of included studies and previous systematic reviews using the snowball method.
Apply key-terms: 'trough', 'levels', 'concentration', 'vancomycin', 'acute kidney injury', 'nephrotoxicity', 'renal failure', 'renal impairment'.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Filter identified articles based on pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria following PRISMA guidelines in three stages.

substeps.instruction: Screen all electronic articles by reading titles and abstracts.
Retrieve full-texts for studies presumed to be eligible.

Include only studies reporting outcomes of interest that meet inclusion criteria (adult patients, treated with vancomycin in hospital/ICU, available initial or maximum trough levels) and do not meet exclusion criteria (age <18, cystic fibrosis, treated outside hospital, renal replacement therapy, kidney transplantation, case-reports, small case-series <10 patients, conference abstracts, posters, animal studies, or non-Latin script alphabets).

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Extract specific study and patient data, with two authors performing the extraction and resolving disagreements by consensus.

substeps.instruction: Extract: year of publication, first author name, study design, eligibility criteria, measurement of initial or maximum trough levels, indication of vancomycin, clinical setting, use of loading dose, patients' age, renal function, co-administration of nephrotoxins, and outcomes of interest (trough levels and AKI incidence).

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias and Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of included studies independently via two authors, resolving disagreements by consensus.

substeps.instruction: Use the Cochrane risk of bias tool for randomized controlled trials (evaluating random sequence generation, blinding, allocation concealment, incomplete outcome, and selective reporting).
Use the ROBINS-I tool for observational studies (evaluating confounding, selection, classification, deviation from intended intervention, missing data, measurement, and reporting of outcomes).
Judge credibility of evidence using the GRADE framework.

steps.title: Perform Data Synthesis and Meta-Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the extracted data using Review Manager 5.3, Open Meta-Analyst, and R software with 95% confidence intervals.

substeps.instruction: Analyze trough levels (measured in mg/L) as a continuous variable among patients with and without AKI (defined by vancomycin consensus, KDIGO, AKIN, or RIFLE guidelines) using a random effects model to provide pooled estimates and prediction intervals.

Apply a dose-response method using linear and non-linear models with restricted cubic splines to graphically depict the relationship between trough levels and AKI risk, assessing linearity with the Wald test.
Perform diagnostic accuracy analysis using a bivariate model for pre-specified cut-offs (15 and 20 mg/L) to calculate sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, and construct a summary ROC curve.
Assess publication bias via visual inspection of funnel plots and statistical tests (regression and rank correlation tests) for homogeneous outcomes including >10 studies.

steps.title: Conduct Subgroup and Sensitivity Analyses
steps.instruction: Perform separate analyses for specific subgroups and sensitivity checks if more than 5 studies are available.

substeps.instruction: Conduct subgroup analysis for: incidence of severe AKI and use of initial vs. maximum trough levels.
Conduct sensitivity analysis for: patients in the intensive care unit.
